claim: The paper studies mixing and size segregation of a binary mixture in a partially filled rotating drum.
quote: size segregation of a binary mixture in a partially filled rotating drum

claim: The proposed mathematical model of material transport accounts for free-surface segregation and predicts the evolving nonuniform distribution of the mixture components.
quote: accounts for the free-surface segregation and predicts the evolving nonuniform

claim: The theoretical distributions predicted by the model are in agreement with the experimental data obtained.
quote: theoretical distributions are in agreement with the experimental data

claim: Models that use the difference in repose angles as the macroscopic parameter entirely determining segregation are unable to describe size segregation, since particles differing only in size have the same angle of repose.
quote: such models are unable to describe size segregation

claim: A practicable macroscopic model of granular body formation is derived by combining a material-independent mathematical model of mass transfer with a phenomenological constitutive relation, the operator of segregation.
quote: material-independent mathematical model of mass transfer with a phenomenological

claim: The operator of segregation relates the granular material composition in the surface flow to the composition of the layer generated at the surface of a growing pile or filling.
quote: The operator of segregation relates the granular material composition

claim: The segregation operator for binary mixtures in which particles differ only in size was identified using Drahun and Bridgwater's experimental data on size segregation in a two-dimensional pile growing under a point source.
quote: identified the segregation operator for the binary mixtures

claim: Although both the configuration and the material of particles in the drum are different from those in the identification experiments, a good agreement of theoretical predictions and experimental data was achieved without any fitting of model parameters.
quote: achieved without any fitting of model parameters

claim: The mixer used in the experiments was a cylindrical vessel of 141 mm internal diameter and 36 mm length, made of transparent plastic and open at one end.
quote: cylindrical vessel, 141 mm in internal diameter and 36 mm in length

claim: Experiments used binary mixtures filling various portions of the drum with various weight ratios of two sizes of spherical particles (d1 = 1.37 mm and d2 = 2.51 mm, standard deviations not exceeding 5%).
quote: various weight ratios of two sizes of spherical particles

claim: All particles were made of zirconium oxide with a material density of 4.14 g/cm3.
quote: made of zirconium oxide with a material density of 4.14 g/cm

claim: The surface flow took place in a thin boundary layer 2-4 particle diameters in thickness and occurred either in avalanches or continuously, depending on the speed of rotation.
quote: occurred either in avalanches or continuously, depending on the speed of rotation

claim: Fines easily find a niche at the lower part of the free surface where they are trapped while larger particles have to roll down further, producing a higher concentration of fines in the central part of the filling.
quote: higher concentration of fines in the central part of the filling

claim: Radial segregation, which appears already at the beginning of rotation, is the main issue of the work; axial segregation is not considered and the consideration is limited to a two-dimensional cross section of the drum.
quote: radial segregation, which appears already at the beginning of rotation

claim: Mathematically, the avalanche mixing model of Metcalfe et al. is a finite difference approximation of a simple continuous flow mixing model.
quote: avalanche mixing in a rotating drum is a finite difference approximation

claim: Although the surface flow in the pile experiments of Drahun and Bridgwater occurred by avalanches, the continuous model was able to predict the resulting size distributions of particles in the pile.

claim: The model neglects the dependence of bulk density and repose angle on material composition and the percolation of small particles through the bulk, which is justified if the particle sizes are not too different.
quote: the dependence of the bulk density and repose angle on material composition

claim: Adding the conservation laws for both components yields the equation for total surface flux, whose solution is J = (omega/2)(a^2 - s^2), with the normal velocity at the free surface V_n = -omega*s.

claim: According to the model, if the drum is more than half full there exists a nonmixing rotating central core of particles which never reach the free surface, though in practice some erosion of this core occurs because of the finite thickness of the surface flow layer.
quote: there exists a nonmixing rotating central core

claim: In the tracer experiments of Drahun and Bridgwater the mean tracer position is not affected by the type of material and depends linearly on the diameter ratio for 0.4 < d1/d2 < 1.6.
quote: mean tracer position is not affected by the type of material

claim: For low concentration of type-1 particles the segregation function is approximated by S = C1*kappa+ with C1 = C(d1/d2); for high concentration by S = 1 - C2*(1 - kappa+); between these limiting cases a smooth monotone parametric interpolation is used.
quote: if the source concentration of type-1 particles is low

claim: Using the thus-identified segregation operator, theoretical tracer distributions close to the experimental ones were obtained for various size ratios, and a good agreement of theoretical and experimental distributions has been obtained in all cases where both types of particles were present in significant quantities.
quote: of theoretical and experimental distributions has been obtained in all cases

claim: In the present work the previously identified operator of segregation is used without any changes to predict the distribution of species in a rotating drum.
quote: identified operator of segregation without any changes

claim: The surface flux concentration of fines at s = 0 exhibits time oscillations whose period depends on the filled drum portion and whose amplitude, determined by the initial material distribution, decreases exponentially as the stationary particle distribution is established.
quote: The period of these oscillations depends on the filled drum portion

claim: In the stationary state the concentration of a component depends only on the distance from the drum axis and equals the surface layer concentration at the corresponding surface point.
quote: depends only on the distance from the drum axis

claim: The stationary radial distribution of material in a 20%-filled drum is the same as in an 80%-filled drum outside the nonmixing core.

claim: In the first series of experiments (drum about 62% filled, samples taken at r = 0.42R and r = 0.83R, total weight portion of fines varying from 10% to 90%), the calculated and experimentally determined sampler concentrations are very close.
quote: calculated and experimentally determined sampler concentrations are very close

claim: In the second series of experiments (total weight concentration of fines 50%, drum either 39% or 56% filled, samples at various distances from the center), the correspondence of theoretical and experimental concentrations is also quite satisfactory.

claim: Since the size segregation operator was identified using data obtained for an entirely different geometric configuration and different materials, the agreement obtained confirms that this operator depends only on the particle diameter ratio.
quote: confirms that this operator depends only on the particle diameter ratio

claim: The theoretical model consists of material transport equations, determined by the problem's geometry, and an operator of surface segregation, a phenomenological relation characterizing the segregation properties of granular material.
quote: an operator of surface segregation, a phenomenological relation

claim: The assumption that the surface flow is confined to a very thin boundary layer limits the applicability of the model to slow rotation.
quote: This limits the applicability of our model to slow rotation

claim: Percolation of fines in the bulk is generally significant only if the fine particles are several times smaller than the large ones or in the presence of vibration; since the diameter ratio was 0.55 in the experiments, no significant percolation in a motionless bulk should be expected.
quote: no significant percolation in a motionless bulk should be expected

claim: Axial segregation in the experiments was not entirely negligible: bands containing a higher proportion of large particles could be observed near the drum ends after only 15-20 revolutions.
